---
title: "Breakout room - First-time visitor"
---

## Scenario

**First-time visitor**:
You’ve been told a dataset is available from Bioconductor.
Can you find it, get it, open it and use it?

### Example dataset

> "Zeisel 2015 is one of the most beloved datasets in the [Orchestrating Single-Cell Analysis with Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA/) (OSCA) book".

Usage in OSCA book: <https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.workflows/zeisel-mouse-brain-strt-seq.html>

Published article: <https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaa1934>

More (single-cell) datasets: <https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/BiocViews.html#___SingleCellData>

## Load R packages

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ExperimentHub))
```

## Browsing the ExperimentHub

### In R

```{r}
hub <- ExperimentHub()

hub
```

### Online

Package: <https://bioconductor.org/packages/BiocHubsShiny/ >

Primary Shiny app: <https://shiny.sph.cuny.edu/app/BiocHubsShiny/>

- HTTPS certificate currently invalid. Request sent to admin.

Alternative Post Connect Cloud instance: <https://link-ny-biochubsshiny.share.connect.posit.cloud>

### Exported to a CSV file

Bioconductor only provides a SQLite file that contains metadata about the datasets available.

Users are expected to interact with it via R functions provided by the *ExperimentHub* package.

The code below exports that table of metadata to a CSV file that you can download and browse in Excel.

```{r}
metadata <- as.data.frame(S4Vectors::mcols(hub))

if (!dir.exists("01-data"))
    dir.create("01-data")

write.csv(metadata, "01-data/ExperimentHub_metadata.csv", row.names = TRUE)
```

Download the output CSV file [here](01-data/ExperimentHub_metadata.csv)

## Activity

Reading [this chapter](https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.workflows/zeisel-mouse-brain-strt-seq.html) of the book "Orchestrating Single-Cell Analysis with Bioconductor", you see that the "Zeisel, 2015" dataset is available from Bioconductor.

The book chapter includes a citation leading to the originl article <https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaa1934>.

### User experience

What information do you require before using the dataset redistributed by Bioconductor?

How much provenance information do you expect Bioconductor to include in its own metadata?

When is it sufficient for Bioconductor to link out to metadata stored elsewhere/upstream?

How far back upstream shoud Bioconductor track provenance metadata? Published count matrices? FASTQ files?

Do you see any gap when tracing data processing steps between the Bioconductor object given to you and the data produced by the experiment?

Where do you look for information? Bioconductor website? Google? Favourite AI chatbot?

How much information (that you care about) can you find out about the dataset without having to install and use R?

How long does it take you to find instructions for accessing the dataset?

How many of the [FAIR criteria](https://www.gofair.foundation/fair-principles) does it pass?

Where are you struggling?

What information is missing from the bioconductor website? what could/should the core team or developers do better?
